clue.text: Legendary figure bringing about illness, suffering and the onset of barbarism

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of barbarism is used

parts.note: first letter B

indicators.note: to bring a boat about is to turn it round, so the pieces are turned into a new order

parts.note: flu is an illness
woe is suffering

explanation.surface: A mythical figure arrives spreading sickness, misery and the first stirrings of savagery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing about' looks like 'causing' but asks you to turn FLU, WOE and B (the onset of barbarism) around into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Beowulf is the hero of the Old English epic poem, slayer of Grendel, a figure of legend.

clue.text: Might one sit on this purse?

definitions.text: Might one sit on this purse?

parts.words: Might one sit on this purse?
parts.note: beans is slang for money, so a purse could be a bag of beans, and you can sit on the soft seat of that name

explanation.walkthrough: A purse is a bag for money, and 'beans' means money as in 'not a bean'; the seat is a large bag of polystyrene beads.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a large soft cushion-seat filled with beads, something people sit on.

clue.text: They are, in the main, army or company retreats with first-class appliances

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so CO is read in reverse

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer in the army, and also the abbreviation for company
top means first-class, the best
uses are applications or appliances of something

explanation.surface: Military or business groups withdraw to plush facilities by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, so the definition is things that live in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopuses live in the ocean, and 'the main' is a poetic term for the sea.

clue.text: Its existence is up in the air

definitions.text: Its existence is up in the air

parts.words: Its existence is up in the air
parts.note: up in the air means uncertain, and also literally flying overhead

explanation.walkthrough: Whether these flying saucers exist at all is doubtful, and if they do they are in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An unidentified flying object is seen in the sky, and whether alien craft are real remains doubtful.

clue.text: Eggs that may be taken on board by Miss Piggy?

definitions.text: Eggs that may be taken on board by Miss Piggy?

parts.words: Eggs that may be taken on board by Miss Piggy?
parts.note: Miss Piggy of the Muppets loves Kermit the frog, so his offspring would be hers to take on

explanation.walkthrough: Miss Piggy's sweetheart is Kermit the Frog, so the eggs she might adopt are a frog's.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogspawn is the mass of jelly-coated eggs laid by frogs in ponds.

clue.text: By 11, they deliver cigarettes

parts.note: the answer to 11 across is BAP, a bread roll
UPS is the American parcel delivery company

explanation.surface: Next to some numbered house, couriers drop off packets of smokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 refers to another clue's answer: a bap is a soft bread roll. 'By' simply sets ROLL beside UPS, the parcel carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Roll-ups are hand-rolled cigarettes made from loose tobacco and papers.

clue.text: With time it will do so

definitions.text: With time it will do so

parts.words: With time it will do so
parts.note: the word time chimes with this word, so it does what the word itself means

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as patience paying off, but 'it will do so' means the answer does to 'time' what it names.
explanation.definitionFit: Time and the answer share the same final sound, so they chime, as verse lines do.

clue.text: £51 cooked roast? Are they wind-up merchants?!

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
quid is slang for a pound

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or altered, so the letters of roast are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joint costing fifty-one pounds: are the butchers having us on?
explanation.walkthrough: A wind-up merchant is British slang for a prankster; here it means someone who winds up companies. The 51 pounds becomes LI QUID.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquidators are appointed to wind up insolvent companies, closing them down and selling their assets.

clue.text: To release docked vessel at last

indicators.note: docked as a tail is docked, cut short at the end

parts.note: to untie is to release

indicators.note: at last means finally, so only the final letter of vessel is used

parts.note: last letter L

explanation.surface: Instructions to free a ship that has finally come into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks nautical beside 'vessel', but it means cut short: UNTIE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'nine to five', to and until both mark the end point of a span of time.

clue.text: Lies about special spinning tools

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of putting a spin on news
awls are pointed tools for piercing holes

explanation.surface: Someone tells falsehoods about some unusual rotating implements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies about' looks like telling untruths, but it means lolling around. 'spinning' gives PR, since spin doctors work in public relations.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to lie with limbs spread out carelessly, lounging around.

clue.text: Harry got royals trying to predict the future

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or ravage, so the letters of got royals are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Prince Harry pestered the royal family while attempting fortune-telling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads as the prince, but it is the verb meaning to harass, the signal to rearrange GOT ROYALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrology claims to foretell events from the positions of stars and planets.

clue.text: A sailor's east of Quebec — here, maybe?

indicators.note: in an across clue east is to the right, so A and the sailor come after the Q

parts.note: Q is Quebec in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman finds himself somewhere east of the Canadian city: perhaps here?
explanation.walkthrough: 'here, maybe?' asks for a place, and the question mark warns it is one example: a Gulf state a sailor might reach far to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatar is a country, one example of a place someone could be referring to as 'here'.

clue.text: Two characters observed outside petrol station eating a bun

indicators.note: one thing eating another holds it inside, so A goes within the two letters

parts.words: Two characters observed outside petrol station
parts.note: BP, the oil company's two letters, are the sign seen outside many British petrol stations

explanation.surface: Someone spotted eating a bun on the forecourt of a filling station.
explanation.walkthrough: BP (British Petroleum) is a major fuel brand whose initials appear on petrol station signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bap is a soft, round bread roll, a type of bun in British usage.

clue.text: Relative entropy is linear, varying in the extremes of tidal-flow

parts.note: S is the standard symbol for entropy in physics

indicators.note: varying means changing, so these letters are rearranged
the extremes are the first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters T and W

explanation.surface: A physics remark: entropy behaves linearly, but deviates at the extremes of a tidal current.
explanation.walkthrough: After S for entropy, the letters of IS LINEAR plus T and W (the ends of tidal-flow) are rearranged as 'varying' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister-in-law is a family member by marriage, so she is one kind of relative.

clue.text: Sponge located on top of mug

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: spotted means located or found
a mug is a fool, and so is a dick in slang

explanation.surface: A sponge left sitting on a coffee cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants, a kind of sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: This traditional British pudding is a steamed sponge studded with currants or raisins.

clue.text: A lot of energy is created by Storm Oscar

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind, a short storm
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A named storm, Oscar, generates enormous power.
explanation.walkthrough: Storms are given personal names in Britain, so 'Storm Oscar' reads as one weather event; split it into GUST and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means great enthusiasm and vigour, a lot of energy put into doing something.

clue.text: Those taking in workers from the colonies?

definitions.text: Those taking in workers from the colonies?

parts.words: Those taking in workers from the colonies?
parts.note: reads like employers recruiting labour from overseas territories, but the workers are ants and the colonies are their nests

explanation.walkthrough: The colonial-labour picture misleads: worker ants live in colonies, and 'taking in' means swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: These animals feed on ants, licking them out of their nests with long sticky tongues.

clue.text: Green tea's brewed for young people

indicators.note: brewing stirs ingredients together, so the letters of Green tea's are mixed up

explanation.surface: Green tea, freshly made, is aimed at youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are adolescents aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Those that bring about death and deal with its aftermath

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old sense of the word is executioners, those who carry out a death sentence
second meaning: people named in a will to administer the dead person's estate

explanation.walkthrough: The archaic sense is someone who executes a criminal; the modern sense executes a will.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one who carries something out, whether a death sentence or the instructions in a will.

clue.text: Rose might be in this old hat, carrying tent back to the start

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the altered tent goes within PASSE

parts.note: passé means old hat, out of fashion

indicators.note: the back letter of tent goes round to the front

explanation.surface: A rose pinned to an outdated hat, with a tent folded back.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower is a false trail: 'rose' is the verb, the past form of rise. 'back to the start' moves the last T of TENT to the front, giving TTEN, which PASSE is 'carrying'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the simple past form of the verb rise, so it is grammatically in that tense.

clue.text: Books footballer's written about Brighton's uneven playing surface

indicators.note: PELES is written around the books, holding them inside

parts.note: Pelé was the great Brazilian footballer
B is an abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Volumes about a footballer describe Brighton's bumpy pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is an English seaside town famous for its stony beach rather than sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton's beach is made of pebbles, an uneven surface for any game played on it.

clue.text: Unused tin-opener to get patent

parts.note: something unused is left over
the opener of tin is its first letter, T

explanation.surface: Spare can-openers might be worth patenting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like the noun for an invention; here it is the adjective meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or open to view, which is what overt means.

clue.text: Bluebird represents this silly-billy with the discontented face of regret

parts.note: a twit is a silly person

indicators.note: with its contents removed, only the outer letters of the remain

parts.note: outer letters T and E

indicators.note: the face is the front, so the first letter

parts.note: first letter R

explanation.surface: The setter Bluebird portrays a fool wearing a sulky, rueful expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluebird is the setter's name, and a blue bird was the logo of the social network.
explanation.definitionFit: The social network Twitter used a small blue bird as its logo for many years.

clue.text: Being indecisive, I rub around desperate cowboy's bottom

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters of I rub are read backwards

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the cowboy of the British comic The Dandy
ass is American slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: Unable to decide, someone massages a frantic cowhand's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a hugely strong cowboy from the long-running British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Buridan's ass is the philosophical donkey that starves between two equal bales of hay, a creature paralysed by indecision.

clue.text: At sea — Côte d'Azur's southernmost point? That's right

parts.note: in a down clue the southernmost point of Azur is its last letter, R

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of Côte are rearranged

explanation.surface: Out on the water off the southern tip of the French Riviera: yes, correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The Côte d'Azur is the French Riviera. 'That's right' reads as agreement, but 'right' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Recto is the right-hand page of an open book, as opposed to verso on the left.

clue.text: Managed to catch Basic Instinct — on reflection, it's the pits

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the result is read backwards
catching means holding, so RAN goes around ID

parts.note: ran means managed
the id is Freud's term for the basic instinctive part of the mind

explanation.surface: Someone got round to watching the film Basic Instinct and, thinking about it, found it terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic Instinct' is a 1992 film, but here it is the id. RAN catching ID gives RIDAN, then 'on reflection' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, which is what 'the pits' means informally.

clue.text: Piece of dripping picked up

indicators.note: picked up as by a microphone, meaning heard rather than seen

parts.note: oozy means seeping or dripping

explanation.surface: A bit of beef fat lifted from the roasting pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of dripping' suggests cooking fat, but 'Piece' alone is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece is slang for a firearm, and the Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun.

clue.text: 'Chili' — irregular or alternative spelling of fruit

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters of Chili are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spelling note: 'chili' is a nonstandard or variant way of writing a fruit's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to discuss spelling chilli; the variant spelling meant is of a different fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichi is a variant spelling of lychee, the sweet white-fleshed Chinese fruit.

clue.text: Mix chopped tomato with sliced bread, though not to make a dish

indicators.note: mixing scrambles these letters into a new order
chopped up, adding to the sense of the letters being broken and rearranged
sliced up, again telling us the letters are cut apart and reordered
says the letters of the following to are left out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: combine diced tomato with bread, but don't actually turn it into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TOMATO and BREAD, without T and O, are rearranged. The cooking picture hides that 'dish' means an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal for a very attractive person, as is dreamboat.

clue.text: Low sound of whisky being tipped over room's contents

parts.note: whisky is W in the NATO alphabet, and W turned upside down is M
the contents of room are its middle letters, OO; that the answer also appears backwards in room is a coincidence

explanation.surface: The glug of a dram being knocked over across a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as quiet, but it is the verb a cow does. 'over' also puts M above OO in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to moo, the deep sound made by cattle.

clue.text: Turned on, artist is playing with balls across the table

definitions.text: playing with balls across the table

indicators.note: turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning
Jeff Koons is an American artist

explanation.surface: An excited artist is fooling around with balls on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' looks like excitement, but 'Turned' reverses RE (on) and KOONS, the artist known for balloon-dog sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue game in which coloured balls are potted across a large baize table.

clue.text: Back from the west of Russia with slightly-damaged spoons

indicators.note: damaged suggests something knocked out of shape, so the letters of spoons are rearranged
the west is the left-hand end of the word, its first letter

parts.note: first letter R

explanation.surface: Someone returns from western Russia carrying dented cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as returning, but it is the verb meaning to support financially.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor someone is to support them financially or publicly, which is to back them.
